clue.text: Meat and toasted cake, no starters, help in reception

indicators.note: the starters of the two foods are their first letters, which are dropped from each

parts.note: heart is offal, eaten as meat
a crumpet is a griddle cake usually eaten toasted

explanation.surface: A menu note recommending meat and toasted cake to whoever is helping at a reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no starters' removes the first letters of both HEART and CRUMPET, leaving EART and RUMPET. 'Reception' here is the reception of sound, not a party.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned horn-shaped hearing aid collects sound, helping a deaf person's reception of speech.

clue.text: Skin layer from duck, breached by pressure spray briefly

indicators.note: the duck's name is broken open by the pressure letter, which sits inside it

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck prized for its down
P is the standard symbol for pressure

indicators.note: a word said briefly is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a mist is a fine spray of droplets

explanation.surface: A skincare instruction about a layer of skin made from duck, pierced by a pressurised spray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' docks MIST to MIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer, protective layer of the skin is called by this anatomical name.

clue.text: Maybe one resisting turnover finds cake on counter

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: a roll is a small bread cake
a bar is the counter where drinks are served

explanation.surface: A business that resists losing turnover sells cake over the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' suggests money or a pastry; here it is a vehicle overturning.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong bar over a vehicle's cab protects occupants if it overturns, so it resists a rollover.

clue.text: Potentially unsportsmanlike bowling hypnotised member

parts.note: someone hypnotised is said to be under
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator calls some bowling unsporting, as if the bowler had a hypnotised arm.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, bowling below the shoulder is famously associated with an unsporting delivery rolled along the ground in a 1981 match.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivering the ball with the hand below shoulder height is the style named, and in cricket it can be seen as unsporting.

clue.text: Turducken perhaps warmed up — or not — at spread

indicators.note: the letters are spread out and rearranged, as on a table

explanation.surface: A turducken, a bird stuffed inside birds, either heated up or not, served at a feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' signals the rearrangement; the dashes make 'or not' look like an aside, but its letters belong to the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Turducken blends turkey, duck and chicken into one coined term, just as such a blend word fuses two or more words.

clue.text: Tablet provided with article about enormous bird

indicators.note: the article goes about, or around, the bird's name

parts.note: the is the definite article
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A stone tablet carved with an article about a giant bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a medicinal lozenge, a small tablet dissolved in the mouth.

clue.text: Bark associated with golden retriever?

parts.note: a bark is a sailing ship, and the golden retriever is Jason, who went to fetch the Golden Fleece, not a dog

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bark' and 'golden retriever' paint a dog; the bark is a vessel and the retriever is Jason fetching the Golden Fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason and his Argonauts sailed in this ship on their quest for the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Hostile to royal household in battle

parts.note: agin is a dialect form of against, meaning opposed to
a court is a monarch's household and retinue

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to the royal household finds themselves in a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry V's English army beat the French at this 1415 battle in northern France.

clue.text: Scientist one found in ship after docking

indicators.note: the numeral one is found in the shortened ship's name
docking cuts off a tail, so the ship's name loses its last letter

parts.note: a galleon is a large sailing ship
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A scientist was found aboard a ship after it docked in port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docking' looks like mooring in harbour; it means cutting a tail, so GALLEON becomes GALLEO before I goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian astronomer and physicist championed the Copernican view of the solar system.

clue.text: Samoan, maybe large, prepared sardine outside

indicators.note: the rearranged fish sits outside, around, the size letter
food that is prepared is worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A Samoan, perhaps a big one, prepares a sardine dish outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges SARDINE to ISANDER, which goes 'outside' L.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoa is a Pacific island nation, so a Samoan is an example of an island dweller.

clue.text: Bird, first in oven, one having stuffed part

indicators.note: the first letter in the word oven is taken
one has stuffed the part, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a role is an actor's part
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A recipe: a bird goes first into the oven, with one part of it stuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one having stuffed part' puts I inside ROLE, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden orioles are brightly coloured songbirds of Europe and Asia.

clue.text: German banker resident in Heidelberg

indicators.note: the letters live inside the city's name

explanation.surface: A German bank employee living in Heidelberg.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is often a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: This major river flows through Germany to the North Sea, and rivers have banks.

clue.text: Decrepit couple going on strike

indicators.note: the couple's word goes on after the strike's word

parts.note: to ram is to strike forcefully
to shackle is to couple or chain together

explanation.surface: A frail old couple decide to go on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple' looks like a pair of people; it is a verb meaning to fasten together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tumbledown or in a state of near collapse is described this way, like decrepit.

clue.text: Fat soldier catching fish

indicators.note: the soldier catches the fish, holding it inside

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving with the navy
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: An overweight soldier goes out fishing and lands a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: This butter substitute is an edible fat used for spreading and baking.

clue.text: Show of charity by saint moved Paul's audience

parts.note: a charity gala is a fundraising show

indicators.note: letters moved around are rearranged

explanation.surface: A charity event staged with a saint moved the audience who heard Paul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges SAINT to TIANS.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul's letter to the churches of Galatia was addressed to these people, his readers.

clue.text: Pleasingly plump beast about to be snared by vagrant

indicators.note: the beast is trapped inside the vagrant's word

parts.note: a bum is a tramp or vagrant

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the beast's word is read backwards

parts.note: an ox is a beast of burden

explanation.surface: A plump animal is about to be trapped by a tramp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'on the point of', but it is the reversal signal; 'to be snared by' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: This describes a woman with a full, attractively rounded figure.

clue.text: Woman dominant in right manner, shown up in game

indicators.note: the reversed pieces go in the game's word

parts.note: a match is a game or contest

indicators.note: in a down answer, shown up means written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: an air is a manner or bearing

explanation.surface: A woman who rightly dominates is exposed during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown up' reverses the letters to RIAR, which goes in the game's word.
explanation.definitionFit: A female head of a family or tribe holds the dominant role in it.

clue.text: Busy hospital in Eton cured one patient

indicators.note: the hospital letter goes in the rearranged school name
something cured is treated and changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
Job, of the Old Testament, is a byword for patience

explanation.surface: A busy hospital at Eton school healed one patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cured' rearranges ETON to ONTE, with H put 'in'. Eton is a famous English boarding school. 'patient' is the adjective: the patience of Job.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at work, actively engaged in a task, is the idiom's sense, like being busy.

clue.text: Follow singular conversation?

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
talk is conversation

explanation.surface: A request to follow a single conversation, perhaps one-sided.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that a one-person talk is no conversation at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue someone stealthily or obsessively is to follow them closely.

clue.text: Alas you're right to use horn on French street!

indicators.note: in a down answer, the hooting word sits on top of the street

parts.note: to toot is to sound a car horn
rue is French for street

explanation.surface: A rueful driver admits that honking in a Paris street is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a remark is all too accurate is a regretful way of agreeing, an idiom of rueful assent.

clue.text: Scot cleaned out in tightest financial investigation

indicators.note: the Scot's outer letters go in the word for tightest

parts.note: tight with money means mean, so tightest is meanest

indicators.note: a word cleaned out has its insides emptied, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: A Scotsman left broke by the tightest of financial checks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleaned out' empties the middle of the word, keeping its outside letters. The surface plays on the stereotype of Scots as thrifty.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an official inquiry into a person's income and savings to decide whether they qualify for state help.

clue.text: Protein and energy supplied to number eleven?

indicators.note: the energy letter is given to the front of the batting term

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
in cricket the number eleven batter is last in to bat

explanation.surface: A nutritionist provides protein and energy to a footballer wearing the number eleven shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting order runs to eleven, so the number eleven batter goes in last.
explanation.definitionFit: This elastic connective-tissue protein lets skin and arteries stretch and recoil.

clue.text: Single-breasted styles to suit this warrior?

definitions.text: Single-breasted styles to suit this warrior?

parts.words: Single-breasted styles to suit this warrior?
parts.note: legend says the women warriors of Greek myth removed one breast to draw a bow, so a single-breasted jacket would fit them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Single-breasted' looks like tailoring; the legend has these warriors with one breast.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these were a race of female warriors, said to have removed one breast.

clue.text: Wines given opening in naval base

parts.note: ports are fortified wines from Portugal
a mouth is an opening

explanation.surface: Wines are offered at an opening ceremony at a naval base.
explanation.definitionFit: This English south-coast city is home to a major Royal Navy dockyard.

clue.text: Present suppliers not entirely brilliant

indicators.note: a word given not entirely is missing its final letter

parts.note: magic is slang for brilliant or wonderful

explanation.surface: Gift suppliers that were not completely brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: The wise men from the East brought gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh to the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Substitute monarch posed with Zulu

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a model who posed for a portrait sat for it
Zulu is the NATO alphabet word for Z

explanation.surface: A stand-in king posed for a portrait alongside a Zulu.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial replacement, often an inferior imitation, is described with this German loan word.

clue.text: See City peak after job changes one opposes

indicators.note: the pieces for the city and peak come after the rearranged job
the word job changes, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a see is a bishop's seat; the City of London, home of St Paul's, has the postcode EC
a tor is a rocky peak, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: An invitation to view a city summit once the work changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges JOB to OBJ. EC is the postcode of the City of London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises an objection is one who opposes a proposal or measure.

clue.text: Graduates find kippers here — tucked in?

definitions.meaning: BEd is the Bachelor of Education degree, so its holders are graduates
kippers are people who kip, or sleep, and they lie tucked in at night

explanation.walkthrough: 'kippers' looks like smoked fish; it is people taking a kip, British slang for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaching degrees name the graduates, and sleepers lie tucked into these pieces of furniture.

clue.text: Sea slug sends horse back with one limb

indicators.note: sent back means the horse's word is read backwards

parts.note: a dun is a horse of greyish-brown colour
I is the Roman numeral for one
a branch is a limb of a tree

explanation.surface: A sea slug dispatches a horse with a single limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses DUN to NUD.
explanation.definitionFit: These shell-less marine molluscs, often vividly coloured, are the familiar sea slugs.
